Any or all keywords. Keyword types (default any)

News sources. news, news_keyword
news: news kinds; dividend: declared / ex_date / payment
Only earnings news. news, news_keyword
Call lifecycle events. earnings_call (transcript_provisional, transcript_corrected, documents_updated need STANDARD; guidance_flash, keyword_hit PRO)
Only these speakers. earnings_call_keyword
Fire at this many mentions. earnings_call_keyword
Only these dividend types. dividend
Halt or resumption (empty = both). halt

Results reports to fire on. earnings_results
The event counted down to. event_countdown

`crosses_*` fire when the price crosses `level`; `above` / `below` also fire at once when the price is already on that side. price
The price level (> 0). price
Which move fires. price_move
The move in percent of the baseline. price_move
What the move is measured from (ignored with window_minutes); gap_open = the session open against the prior close, once per session. price_move
Measure the move against the price this many minutes ago instead of the baseline. price_move

`relative` = a closed bar's volume ≥ multiple × its baseline; `absolute` = ≥ threshold; `session` = today's cumulative volume ≥ multiple × the 20-session average daily volume (US stocks). volume_spike
The bar evaluated at its close. volume_spike (1h, 1d, 1w, 1mo); script and indicator (1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h, 1d; the plan's shortest: FREE / LITE 1h, STANDARD 5m, PRO 1m)
Volume multiple of the baseline (relative / session). volume_spike
Bar volume threshold, > 0 (absolute). volume_spike
Bars in the baseline, 5–200 (rvol_slot: sessions, 2–20). volume_spike
The volume baseline: the mean or the median of the previous bars, or `rvol_slot` = the mean of the same time-of-day bar of earlier sessions (default flat_mean). volume_spike
Only bars that closed up / down (default any). volume_spike

The instant of a `once` reminder (ISO 8601 date-time with offset, e.g. 2026-12-01T14:30:00Z). price_reminder
Day of a weekly reminder, 0 = Sunday. price_reminder
Several weekdays (0 = Sunday) of a daily / weekly reminder. price_reminder
The script version evaluated (`scv_…`, status ok, of a script of this account). script
Only these of the script's alerts (its version's `alert_ids`); empty = all. script
`once` = the alert becomes `triggered` after its first fire (default every_time)
Minimum seconds between fires

The alert becomes `triggered` after this many fires
The alert becomes `expired` then (ISO 8601 date-time with offset, e.g. 2026-12-01T14:30:00Z)

The alert is `scheduled` until then (ISO 8601 date-time with offset, e.g. 2026-12-01T14:30:00Z)
No fires until then (ISO 8601 date-time with offset, e.g. 2026-12-01T14:30:00Z)

params.name: company
params.description: Ticker (`AAPL`) or CIK (all digits, any padding); a comma list of 1–50 reads several companies in one request (R2). Required. US ETFs: a fund registrant such as SPY and a series of a multi-series trust such as TQQQ both resolve on `/v1/dividends`, `/v1/splits` and `/v1/filings` (a trust series' filings are the accessions naming its series; an ETF that is its own registrant lists its registrant's; a row's `company.cik` is the trust's CIK, empty for an ETF without a registrant link). The company-only families (financials, metrics, segments, fiscal periods, insider trades, events, transcripts, guidance, people, investor documents, IPOs) answer one 404 `not_covered` naming the ETF ("TQQQ is an ETF: … exists only for companies"); on the other lists a series ETF such as TQQQ is not a known company.

params.name: sort

params.name: offering_id
params.description: Offering id: the Form D file number, or the first accession number of an offering whose filings state none

params.name: company
params.description: Issuer: a CIK (all digits, any padding; any Form D issuer, listed or not) or the ticker of a listed company — ONE value; matches the primary issuer and co-issuers. Without it: every offering

params.name: filed_at.gte
params.description: Latest filing on or after this date

params.name: filed_at.lte
params.description: Latest filing on or before this date

params.name: exemption
params.description: Offerings claiming this exemption, as filed (06b, 06c, 04, 3C.7, …)

params.name: industry
params.description: Industry group as filed (case-insensitive exact match)

params.name: total_sold.gte
params.description: Total amount sold at least this many USD

params.name: is_amendment
params.description: true = offerings whose latest filing is an amendment (D/A); false = an original Form D

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort field: `-filed_latest` (the only order the store serves); the offering id tiebreaker is always appended

params.name: company
params.description: Ticker (`AAPL`) or CIK (all digits, any padding); a comma list of 1–50 reads several companies in one request (R2). One of the scope filters of this list is required. US ETFs: a fund registrant such as SPY and a series of a multi-series trust such as TQQQ both resolve on `/v1/dividends`, `/v1/splits` and `/v1/filings` (a trust series' filings are the accessions naming its series; an ETF that is its own registrant lists its registrant's; a row's `company.cik` is the trust's CIK, empty for an ETF without a registrant link). The company-only families (financials, metrics, segments, fiscal periods, insider trades, events, transcripts, guidance, people, investor documents, IPOs) answer one 404 `not_covered` naming the ETF ("TQQQ is an ETF: … exists only for companies"); on the other lists a series ETF such as TQQQ is not a known company.
